key_insight: Deep learning identified retinal fluorescence lifetime signals associated with type 2 diabetes, with modest classification performance beyond age alone.
clinical_relevance: This study concerns diabetes classification—not cancer drug discovery—and suggests a potential research role for retinal metabolic imaging, not a validated diagnostic tool.
method: Generated corrected mean fluorescence lifetime maps from FLIO retinal scans.
Compared CNN, ResNet-18, and XGBoost models across three-class and binary glycemic classification tasks.
Evaluated age-adjusted group differences and compared FLIO models with age-only and FLIO-plus-age models.
evidence_signal: Among 1,783 AI-READI participants, the CNN achieved AUROC 0.60 ± 0.04 for three-class classification versus 0.51 ± 0.03 for age alone, and 0.67 ± 0.04 for normal versus diabetic classification.
watch_item: The cross-sectional analysis and modest discrimination do not establish clinical utility; external validation is not reported in the supplied abstract.
paper_title: Deep Learning of Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Ophthalmoscopy for Type 2 Diabetes Classification
